items.text: Idaho has no medical or adult-use cannabis: the state Office of Drug Policy says using or selling marijuana for any purpose is illegal. Possessing 3 ounces (about 85 g) or less is a misdemeanour with a minimum fine of US$300 for adults (about A$426 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026); more than 3 ounces is a felony (Idaho Code 37-2732). Idaho's definition covers any cannabis extract or preparation containing THC, and hemp products above 0.3% delta-9 THC can be prosecuted as marijuana. Cannabis bought legally in a neighbouring state is still illegal once in Idaho.

laws.rule: Idaho bans using a hand-held mobile electronic device while driving, including at brief stops at traffic lights or stop signs (Idaho Code 49-1401A, from 1 July 2020). Hands-free and voice-operated use, including hands-free navigation, is allowed; hand-held use is allowed only when the vehicle is stopped outside a travel lane, or in an emergency.
laws.penalty_signal: US$75 for a first offence, US$150 for a second and US$300 for later ones within three years (about A$107, A$213 and A$426 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026), plus court costs (US$131.50 in total for a first offence); licence suspension of up to 90 days after three convictions in three years
